Game Boy Color in Atomic Purple

Nintendo’s colour handheld in translucent purple plastic, which shows its circuit board, speaker, and button contacts through the shell.

Source
Wikimedia Commons: Game-Boy-Color-Purple.jpg (Evan-Amos)
Creator

Style
Y2K aesthetic (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods

Evidence
Inspected Evan-Amos’s 2011 photograph of one Atomic Purple unit (Commons, original 1580 × 2580; viewed at 960 × 1568) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored. The photographed unit is privately owned; no museum copy was found.

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Wikipedia says the Game Boy Color launched in Japan on 21 October 1998 and in North America on 18 November 1998. “Atomic Purple”, made from translucent purple plastic, was released at the same time as the other launch colors. Wikipedia: Game Boy Color.

Observed

  • The whole shell is translucent lilac-purple. The green circuit board, the round speaker with its copper coil, screws, and contact pads show through it.
  • A black glass panel frames a gray screen. Below it “GAME BOY” is in gray italic capitals and “COLOR” in red, purple, green, yellow, and blue letters.
  • The buttons are dark gray; the A and B buttons are round and the Select and Start buttons are pill shapes.
  • Every outer corner of the case is rounded.

Why it belongs

Translucency here is a display of the machine itself: the inner technology becomes decoration. This is a central Y2K idea, shared with the iMac G3.

Clear purple is a frequent Y2K candy color; it sits between the blues and the pinks of the palette.

Borrow

Show structure through a tinted translucent surface instead of hiding it.

Use pill-shaped secondary controls next to round primary controls.
